title: Choose Syncrona's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Swiss railway timetable. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Station Timetable
options.lineage: Swiss railway timetables and station departure boards
options.thesis: Your day set like a departure board: every task, event and payment has a time, a line and a status.
options.viewport: Dark board-coloured nav rail; on white, a big condensed date and clock, a 'Next up' departures table (time · line badge · item · status) cut by a red now-line, and a month-spend strip against your threshold.
options.risk: Shades into a costume of a train station if the line badges and red are used outside the jobs they do.

raised.raise: Rank is carried by one family's width axis: condensed for times, dates and money, normal width for prose. No second display face.
Every summary number is shown next to the rows that make it up; no orphan counters on the today view.
Status is a mark in a fixed column: hollow is open, filled is done, red strikes overspend, never colour alone.
Completed tasks stay in their row, struck with the time they were done; nothing silently disappears.
Fixed registration: every calendar day uses the same slots in the same place, so days compare at a glance.

options.label: Rapid Log
options.thesis: One notation for everything: • task, ○ event, – note, ₹ spend, × done, written into a daily log.
options.viewport: Today's daily log as one continuous list of signified entries, the month spread beside it with spend in the margin.
options.risk: Familiar: journaling apps land here often, and the current UI already uses a dot-grid background.

options.label: Terminal Wayfinding
options.thesis: Only the next decision, signed big: what's next, how long until it, where to go after.
options.viewport: A yellow band across the top: next item and minutes until it at monumental scale; the rest of the day as quieter bands below.
options.case: Holds product clarity (a planner's job is 'what's next'), but loses on audience: it reads as an airport, not a personal tool.
options.risk: Yellow everywhere tires fast on screens people use daily, and it leaves little room for the calendar and money.

options.label: Type Specimen
options.thesis: A planner whose rank is pure type scale.
options.viewport: A single huge date numeral with the day's items set small beneath.
options.case: Loses both axes: planners don't identify with a foundry, and sliders have no job here.
options.kept: Rank by one family's width axis instead of extra fonts.

options.label: Ticket Wallet
options.thesis: Each task a coupon that tears off when done.
options.viewport: A wallet of coupon rows for today.
options.case: Loses both: coupons misread tasks as bookings, and stamps add noise to a list.
options.kept: Done items stay visible, marked rather than removed.

options.label: Timetable Slide Rack
options.lineage: pocket airline timetables on a light table
options.thesis: One type size, raked glass slides.
options.viewport: Raked slides of the day's schedule.
options.case: Loses both: raked containers and one type size fight scanning on a working screen.
options.kept: Status as a mark in a fixed cell.

options.label: Monochrome Product
options.thesis: Neutral greys and one accent, every claim with proof.
options.case: Loses both: it is the generic SaaS look you asked to avoid.
options.kept: Every number shown beside the rows that prove it.

options.label: Botanical Folio
options.thesis: Tasks traced through stages like a plant through seasons.
options.viewport: Five plates of the week on one baseline.
options.case: Loses both: no audience link, and the metaphor hides the data.
options.kept: Fixed registration so days compare at a glance.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean productivity dashboard like Linear or Todoist, executed impeccably.
canonCard.viewport: Greeting, three stat cards, today's tasks and upcoming events in panels.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the competition by design.
